brief: A file organizer as a spatial canvas — documents arranged by topic proximity, not lists or grids

dominant_strengths: Colorful file-type badges (PDF/CSV/PNG/SVG) provide instant scannable identity and add controlled chromatic variety against neutrals
Topic clusters with labeled containers (RESEARCH, DESIGN, BUSINESS) frame the spatial metaphor and give regions semantic weight
Card typography hierarchy is clean — title, meta line, and tag chips read in a coherent three-tier rhythm
dominant_weaknesses: Cards overlap clusters chaotically (CSV card straddling Research/Business) without visible relational logic — looks like accidental drag, not intent
Promised 'topic proximity' connections are nearly invisible; only one faint line hints at relationships, undermining the spatial-canvas thesis
Empty top-left toolbar and lone bottom-right rectangle feel unfinished, breaking canvas balance and signaling layout debt
fix_priorities: Make proximity meaningful: add subtle connection lines, gravity wells, or density gradients so spatial position visibly encodes topic similarity
Resolve overlap semantics — either snap cards inside one cluster, or use overlap to denote shared tags with clear visual treatment
Finish the chrome: populate or remove the orphan rectangle and clarify the toolbar icons with labels/tooltips
Introduce a minimap or zoom affordance so the canvas scales beyond a dozen documents
rationale.norman_balance: Reflective concept (spatial filing) outpaces visceral polish and behavioral clarity — users would admire the idea before trusting the interaction.
rationale.intent_fit: Partially solves the brief: clusters exist, but proximity is asserted by labels rather than demonstrated through spatial/visual relationships.
